Theme

Money, work & business · Household, washing & chores

rent verb

pay to use; let out

also rent out, let, hire, rent a flat, rent a car, rented, to let

classical

Cic. Cael. 18: condūxit in Palātiō nōn magnō domum
Traupman 370; 215: autoraedam condūcere, to rent a car

condūcō, condūcere, condūxī, conductum

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

rent, hire (as the tenant or hirer)

The one who pays condūcit, the owner locat. A rented house is domus conductīcia (Lewis & Short s.v. conductīcius).

Other words

  • locō, locāre, locāvī, locātum — rent out, let

    verb, first conjugation · classical · Plin. Ep. 9.37.3: sī nōn nummō sed partibus locem, if I let (the farms) not for money but for a share of the crop; Traupman 370: locāre, to rent out · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Also to give out a job on contract; whoever takes it on condūcit (see contractor).

Examples

  • in omnīque rē contrahendā, vēndundō emendō, condūcendō locandō, vīcīnitātibus et cōnfīniīs, aequum, facilem, multa multīs dē suō jūre cēdentem

    in every bargain, selling and buying, renting and letting, as a neighbour and over boundaries, (he should be) fair and easy, giving up much of his right to manyCic. Off. 2.64

  • cum domus patris ā forō longē abesset, quō facilius et nostrās domūs obīre et ipse ā suīs colī posset, condūxit in Palātiō nōn magnō domum

    since his father’s house was a long way from the Forum, so that he could visit our houses more easily and be visited by his own friends, he rented a house on the Palatine, at no great priceCic. Cael. 18

  • In quā domō habitat? — In quādam conductītiā. — Eho, nūllamne habet propriam domum? — Habet quidem, sed eam locat quibusdam inquilīnīs.

    What house does he live in? — A rented one. — What, hasn’t he a house of his own? — He has, but he lets it to some tenants.Cord. Coll. 2.26

See also rent, landlord, tenant, lend, contractor.
